newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil dismisses report of $5.0 bln trade gap.
newsitem.headline: Brazil dismisses report of $5.0 bln trade gap.

text.p: The Brazilian Finance Ministry dismissed a weekend newspaper report saying economic officials saw a $5.0 billion trade gap in 1997.
A ministry spokesman said the figures given in the Folha de Sao Paulo newspaper Sunday were not official.
"These types of predictions do not exist in this ministry," he said. "They are not official figures."
Folha wrote that economic officials foresaw a $2.0-3.0 billion trade deficit this year followed by a $5.0 billion trade gap in 1997.

It also said that officials were forecasting a 3.5 percent of gross domestic product operational public sector deficit in 1996, dropping to 2-2.5 percent in 1997, and that economic growth would reach 5.0 percent next year.
The government previously steered clear of concrete forecasts, but officials say privately that the trade gap is not expected to exceed $2.0 billion this year.
Finance Minister Pedro Malan has said the government aims this year to halve last year's 5.0 percent operational deficit.
Malan also said he expects this year's economic growth to be better than last year's 4.2 percent and next year's to be even better.
